# coderforge_machines (Data Source)

Every machine the token can see.

This is the list endpoint, which reports identity and state but not hardware; use the `coderforge_machine` data source for the details of one machine.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every machine Terraform is allowed to see. Machines owned by a container
# service are excluded unless include_owned is set, since those must not be
# managed directly.
data "coderforge_machines" "all" {}

# Only the ones that are up.
data "coderforge_machines" "running" {
  state = "running"
}

output "machine_names" {
  value = data.coderforge_machines.all.names
}

output "running_count" {
  value = length(data.coderforge_machines.running.machines)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `include_owned` (Boolean) Include machines owned by another resource, such as container service nodes. Defaults to `false`, since those must not be managed directly.
- `state` (String) Return only machines in this state, such as `running`.

### Read-Only

- `machines` (Attributes List) The matching machines. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--machines))
- `names` (List of String) Names of the matching machines, convenient for `for_each`.

<a id="nestedatt--machines"></a>
### Nested Schema for `machines`

Read-Only:

- `managed_by` (String)
- `name` (String)

- `state` (String)
